A model whose «weights» can be downloaded: you can use it on your own computer or server without paying anyone (respecting its license).
The file with everything the model has learned. If they're «open», anyone can download them.
The piece of text an AI works with (roughly ¾ of a word). APIs charge per million tokens.
A door for programs to use AI directly, paying for what they consume. It's what developers use.
The model's internal «connections». More parameters usually means more capability, but also more memory and cost.
The memory of the graphics card (GPU). It decides which models you can run on your computer: the bigger the model, the more VRAM it needs.
The graphics card. It's the component that runs AI models on a computer.
A score that comes from thousands of blind votes between two results, as in chess: higher = people prefer it more.
The terms of use of an open model: some allow everything (Apache, MIT) and others forbid commercial use.
A standard test to measure and compare models independently.
The models that nothing beats on both quality and price at once: they're the best options for each budget.
Compressing a model (for example to 4 bits) so it takes up less memory, losing a little quality.
How much text the AI can take into account at once (the conversation, attached documents…).
Turning texts or images into lists of numbers to search by meaning. Used for search engines and recommendations.
A model that reorders a list of results to put the most relevant ones first.
Whether a model is already proven: how many independent evaluations have measured it and how long it has been available.
How much it's really used: monthly downloads, popularity on OpenRouter or likes on Hugging Face.
The website where most open models are published and downloaded.
A service that gives API access to hundreds of models; it publishes rankings of the most used ones.
The «brain» of an AI: the file with everything it has learned. Each app (ChatGPT, Claude…) uses one or more models.
The app or website where you talk to an AI model, like ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Le Chat.
Running the model on your own machine or server instead of using another company's service.
